idiom_name: collections.abc.Sequence (or MutableSequence/UserList) wrapper; frozen dataclass when it must not change
implementation_notes: collections.abc.Sequence carries the protocol: implement __len__ and __getitem__ and the ABC's mixins supply __contains__, __iter__, __reversed__, index and count, so for-loops, `in`, reversed() and slicing keep working without re-implementing container behaviour; MutableSequence expresses append/extend/pop/remove in terms of insert and __delitem__. Keep the backing sequence private - a single leading underscore is the only hint Python offers - and hand out tuple(self._items), an iterator or a copy for reads, never the list itself; a tuple is the cheapest read-only snapshot. When the collection must not change at all, prefer a frozen dataclass (or a plain tuple) over a mutable wrapper: @dataclass(frozen=True) raises FrozenInstanceError on attribute writes and, with eq=True, restores hashability.
pitfalls: A property returning self._items, a list, re-opens the collection; return tuple(self._items), an iterator or a new Sequence instance.
Storing the caller's list in __init__ keeps the caller's reference live: later writes through it change the collection's state without passing its methods.
Sequence mixins call __getitem__ per element, so index() and count() are O(n) each on a large wrapper; override them if the payload is large.
UserList is a ready-made wrapper but publishes .data, a plain list, and subclassing list directly exposes every mutating method; both defeat the invariants.
